name: topcoat
description: A batteries-included framework for building web apps
one_liner: An all-in-one toolkit for building fast, reliable websites and web apps in the Rust programming language, bundling the database, routing, and page-rendering pieces developers usually have to wire together themselves.
buyer: A Rust-focused development shop that wants to deliver web apps for clients faster by not reassembling the same backend plumbing on every project.
business_use_cases: A boutique Rust dev agency standardizes all client projects on this framework, cutting project setup time and quoting lower fixed-price builds.
A performance-sensitive SaaS (e.g. a real-time analytics dashboard) is built and sold using it to differentiate on speed and reliability versus slower competitors.
A technical educator sells a paid course teaching web developers to build production Rust apps using this framework as the on-ramp.

money_ideas.idea: Fixed-price web app builds for clients, using this framework to deliver faster than custom-stack competitors
Paid course or bootcamp teaching developers production Rust web development with this framework

steal_this: This is a developer framework, not an end-user product — the real opportunity is positioning a dev shop around it, not selling it directly to non-technical buyers.
